Cyber Attack Disrupts Bulgaria’s Electric Utilities, Affecting Operations at Major Providers

SOFIA, June 19 — A large-scale cyber attack disrupted operations across Bulgaria’s electric utilities industry on Wednesday, with state-owned Bulgarian Energy Holding EAD and several private power providers reporting significant IT outages and delays in customer services.

The incident, believed to be a ransomware attack, began early in the morning and was ongoing at the time of reporting. According to the Bulgarian Association of Electric Utilities, at least four major utility firms were affected, prompting emergency measures to secure critical infrastructure and restore control over compromised systems.

“Several of our member companies, including Bulgarian Energy Holding EAD, have experienced severe disruptions to their IT and billing systems,” said Irena Stoyanova, spokesperson for the trade group. “While power generation and distribution have continued without interruption, customer service centers and digital payment portals are down, causing inconvenience for thousands of households.”

An official from the Ministry of Energy, who requested anonymity due to the ongoing investigation, confirmed that the attack had encrypted key business data and disabled remote access to internal platforms, making it difficult for staff to process new service requests or respond to customer inquiries.

Bulgarian Energy Holding EAD issued a statement acknowledging the incident, saying, “Our technical teams are working with national cybersecurity authorities and outside experts to isolate affected servers and restore normal operations as quickly as possible. No evidence of a breach in operational control systems has been detected so far.”

In Sofia and other major cities, customers reported difficulties in accessing online accounts, paying bills electronically, or reporting outages through automated channels. Some call centers have switched to manual processes, resulting in long waiting times.

“There’s no immediate risk to electricity supply, but the attack highlights the vulnerability of our industry’s digital infrastructure,” said Georgi Petrov, an energy analyst based in Sofia. “Many utilities have digitized their customer interfaces and management systems in recent years, making them more attractive targets for cybercriminals.”

Authorities have not released details on the perpetrators or whether a ransom demand has been received. The National Cybersecurity Directorate said in a statement that “all necessary steps are being taken to contain the impact and support affected companies.”

The Association of Electric Utilities urged customers to be patient and avoid attempting online transactions until further notice. The incident marks one of the most significant cyber attacks on Bulgaria’s energy sector in recent years.
